title: Variable-length coalescer with prefill prioritization and quantile bucketing
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Goal: Reduce padding waste and tail-latency variance by coalescing incoming requests into micro-batches using a quantile-based bucketing strategy that prioritizes prefill requests. This ticket scopes a runtime coalescer that groups variable-length requests while emitting kernel-selection hints and prefill-priority scheduling so the serving stack can choose attention kernels and prefill vs decode order to improve throughput and p95 latency without increasing model quality regressions.
background: Current continuous-batching is sequence-length agnostic in many hotspots. We observe 18-27% padding overhead on mixed workloads, KV cache eviction churn during interleaved prefill/decode, and occasional p95 latency spikes when a long prefill arrives during a short-decode-heavy window. Existing solutions (simple length bucketing or static thresholds) either increase queueing latency or fragment micro-batches and yield suboptimal kernel utilization on GPUs. We propose a quantile-driven variable-length coalescer that learns recent request-length distribution and forms micro-batches at configured quantiles (e.g., 50th/75th/90th), with a prefill priority lane and kernel-hint tags attached to batches.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce average token-level padding by >= 20% on mixed-seqlen synthetic benchmark (mix: 60% short, 30% mid, 10% long)
p95 latency for short-request SLOs improves or remains within 5% of baseline under production-like concurrency
No regression in decoder throughput for long sequences (>1024) beyond 10% under peak load
Coalescer emits kernel_hint tag used by runtime kernel selection at least 95% of the time for formed batches
Rollout plan and kill-switch implemented; ability to disable coalescer per instance/region
tasks: Design quantile estimator and sliding-window sampler for request-length distribution
Implement coalescer module with: multi-lane queues (prefill-priority, normal), quantile bucket selectors, max-latency cap per bucket
Integrate kernel_hint metadata: {"preferred_kernel": string, "estimated_seqlen": int} (serialized as header)
Add tests: unit + end-to-end load test harness using existing synthetic traffic generator
Measure and record metrics: padding_ratio, avg_microbatch_size, p50/p95 latency per seqlen-bin, tokens/sec, kv_cache_miss_rate
Add feature flags and runtime config: quantile thresholds, prefill_priority_enabled, max_wait_ms
Telemetry + dashboard: create console dashboard showing padding savings and kernel_hint adoption rate
Run staged canary rollout in eu-west-1 for 48h with traffic mirroring and revert plan
decisions: Use quantile buckets (dynamic: Q50/Q75/Q90) rather than fixed-length bins to adapt to workload drift
Implement prefill-priority lane: prefill requests bypass normal queueing within configured max_wait to avoid KV-cache thrash for active sessions
Expose kernel_hint to runtime but keep it advisory; runtime may override based on resource availability
Max micro-batch wait cap set to 8ms by default to balance throughput vs latency for short requests
tradeoffs: Tighter quantiles reduce padding but increase scheduling complexity and potential head-of-line blocking for rare long requests
Prefill-priority reduces decode latency for active sessions but may slightly increase average time-to-first-token for non-prefill requests under extreme load
Kernel-hints improve kernel packing but add metadata and coordination complexity between scheduler and executor layers
implementation_notes: Coalescer will be implemented in the fronting request router component to minimize IPC between processes
Use reservoir sampling on a 30s sliding window for quantile estimation to limit memory and provide quick adaptation
Batch header schema will be extended with a small binary blob for kernel_hint to avoid expensive JSON parsing in hot path
Provide a fallback path: if kernel_hint not present or kernel busy, runtime uses existing kernel selection heuristics
tests_and_benchmarks: Create synthetic workload configs: short-heavy, mixed, long-heavy; run each at 70%, 85%, 95% cluster utilization
Compare against baseline: current continuous-batcher and static-length bucketing (existing ENG-4721 configs)
Measure padding_ratio, p50/p95 latency by seqlen-bin, kernel utilization (SM utilization on GPU), and cost-per-100k-tokens
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed comparing reservoir vs t-digest quantile estimators. Reservoir chosen for simplicity and stable tail estimates in 30s window.
2026-02-20: Prototype implemented; observed 22% padding reduction on mixed synthetic workload but p95 for short requests increased by 6% without prefill-priority enabled.
2026-03-02: Added prefill-priority lane and max_wait cap; short-request p95 now within 2% of baseline while retaining 18% padding savings.
2026-03-08: Integration test found mis-serialized kernel_hint in rare paths; fix pushed in PR 3389 and unit tests added.
2026-03-10: Canary deploy queued for eu-west-1; monitoring dashboards prepped. Rollout window 48h with automatic rollback on p95 > baseline + 10% or padding_ratio regression < 10% improvement.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary on canary-cluster with 5% mirrored traffic for 24h
Stage 2: small customer bucket in eu-west-1 (opt-in) for 48h with manual review
Stage 3: gradual ramp to 50% region traffic over 72h, monitor p95 and padding savings
Rollback: instant kill-switch for coalescer module; runtime falls back to continuous-batcher
fallback_policies: If kernel_hint_adoption_rate < 70% for 10m, disable kernel_hint emission and continue coalescing
If p95_latency short-requests > baseline + 10% for 5m, disable prefill-priority lane
If padding savings < 10% for 15m at target load, revert to previous bucketing config
